findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId
isAccessTokenId() matcher has wrong substring offset and inverted boolean logic, making it a no-op check
findings.body:
The new helper `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` is supposed to verify that the grant-type shortcut encoded in the access token id matches the expected grant. Two bugs make this check ineffective:
1. Wrong offset: the encoded context is laid out as sessionType(2 chars) + tokenType(2 chars) + grantType(2 chars), so the grant shortcut occupies index 4-6, but the code extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which actually reads the last char of the tokenType plus the first char of the grantType – never the real grant shortcut.
2. Inverted logic: even if the offset were correct, the code does `if (... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` – i.e. it treats a *matching* shortcut as a failed match, and anything that does NOT match falls through to `return isUUID().matches(items[1])`, which ignores the grant check entirely.
Combined, this matcher effectively never fails on the grant-type portion of the token id (it only checks that the raw-id portion is a UUID), so all the test assertions added in this PR (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) do not actually verify that the correct grant-type shortcut was encoded into the token id, defeating the purpose of the new test coverage.

findings.title: Javadoc claims shortcuts are usually 3 characters, but implementation hard-requires exactly 2
findings.body: The Javadoc for `getShortcut()` states: "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants". However, every built-in implementation in this PR (ac, cc, ci, dg, pc, pg, ro, rt, te) uses exactly 2 characters, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-codes the expectation that the encoded prefix is exactly 6 characters (2 for session type + 2 for token type + 2 for grant type), throwing `IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6")` otherwise. A third-party implementor following the documented "3-letters" guidance would produce tokens that encode successfully (encodeTokenId has no length check) but fail to decode later, since nothing enforces/validates the 2-character contract. The documentation should state the actual required length (2 chars), and ideally the implementation should validate it.

findings.title: New mandatory getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface with no default implementation. Any existing custom/third-party implementation of this provider factory (a supported SPI extension point, registered via META-INF/services) will fail to compile/deploy against this version until it implements the new method. Additionally, if such an implementation is updated hastily and returns null for the shortcut, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` will call `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantName)` on a `ConcurrentHashMap`, which throws `NullPointerException` at server startup (postInit), bringing down the whole realm/session factory initialization rather than failing gracefully for just that custom provider.

findings.title: Removal of public copy constructor Context(Context) is a binary/source compatibility break
findings.body: The previous version of `OAuth2GrantType.Context` had a public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` that cloned all fields from another Context instance. This PR removes that constructor entirely (per the diff) in favor of recomputing `grantType` only in the main constructor. Since `Context` is a public nested class in a provider-facing API, removing a public constructor without deprecation is a backward-incompatible change for any code (including third-party extensions of OAuth2GrantType/OAuth2GrantTypeBase) that relied on cloning a Context via this constructor; such code will now fail to compile.

findings.title: No validation that registered grant shortcuts are non-null and exactly 2 characters long
